biography.plain_text: Indonesian entrepreneur Andi Syamsuddin Arsyad is widely known as Haji Isam. After working as a driver and heavy-equipment operator, he learned mine management and used borrowed capital to rent machinery for coal contracting. That venture grew into Jhonlin Group, whose mining base later supported expansion into logistics, palm-oil processing, biodiesel and sugar.

long_biography.plain_text:
Coal contracting gave Haji Isam his start in business. Known publicly as Haji Isam, Andi Syamsuddin Arsyad worked as a driver and heavy-equipment operator before learning mine management from a local entrepreneur. Borrowed capital allowed him to rent machinery and take on contracting work, forming the enterprise that became Jhonlin Group.

The South Kalimantan group developed beyond coal into logistics and palm-oil processing. Later projects added biodiesel and sugar manufacturing, extending the business from extraction and transport into downstream industry. He remains Jhonlin's founder and chairman. The arc from operating machinery to organising a mining contractor, then building processing and distribution capacity, defines his business career.

The official presidential transcript directly equates Andi Syamsuddin Arsyad with Haji Isam, but the input name components were preserved because reporting is inconsistent about spelling and order.
